paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when the walls close in, who do you lean on? Asa had help before. Hanani reminds him that when he relied on the LORD, God "delivered them into your hand" (2 Chronicles 16:8), even against a vast army with many chariots. But this time Asa reached for silver and gold and a king in Damascus instead. I know the feeling. The first thing I reach for is my own plan, and the LORD is somewhere around number nine on the list.

Now listen to this, because it's the heart of the whole thing. Hanani says, "For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him." (2 Chronicles 16:9). God isn't looking for a perfect record. He's looking for hearts that are fully devoted to Him. Then He wants to show Himself strong for them. That's an open invitation, baker!

The sad part is that Asa kept leaning the wrong way. He got enraged at the hard word, and even in his illness he sought only the physicians and not the LORD (2 Chronicles 16:10, 12). Here's what I take from that: a hard word from God's messenger is a gift, not an attack. So when trouble shows up, go to the LORD first. Let your plans and your helpers come second. Then every sealed box you bake stays warm with trust in Him.
